references.text: Isaiah describes a similar state of spiritual blindness where the people hear but do not understand, and see but do not perceive, which parallels Jesus' claim that those who claim to see actually carry a fixed sin.

John 3:19-20 expands on the theme that the light has come into the world, but people loved darkness instead of light because their deeds were evil. Those who do wrong hate the light and will not come to it, which explains why the Pharisees' claim to 'see' results in their sin remaining.

This verse quotes directly from Isaiah 6:9-10 to explain why many did not believe in Jesus, emphasizing that their ability to see is blocked by a God-sent blindness, just like the Pharisees in chapter 9.

Paul refers to the same prophecy that God has given them a spirit of slumber, eyes that do not see and ears that do not hear, confirming that the spiritual blindness which makes sin persistent is a recurring biblical theme.

In Matthew, Jesus explains that he speaks in parables precisely because those who see do not see, and those who hear do not hear, a direct parallel to the conclusion in John 9 that self-righteousness leads to fixed sin.
